info.title: aprscli
info.description: APRS.NET command-line tool: listen to APRS-IS, parse and replay packets, send as your callsign, serve a feed to local APRS-IS clients, and compute passcodes.

options.name: --help
options.description: Show help and usage information

options.name: --version
options.description: Show version information

commands.name: listen
commands.description: Connect to APRS-IS and stream raw packet lines.

options.name: --callsign
options.description: Login callsign, with optional SSID. Default: a listener ID such as SWL482913, which logs in to receive only.

options.name: --passcode
options.description: APRS-IS passcode. Default: -1 (read-only). Prefer the APRS_PASSCODE environment variable; an option value is visible in the process list and your shell history. Never printed or logged.

options.name: --server
options.description: Server as host[:port]. Cannot be combined with --region, --port or --full-feed when it includes a port. Default: rotate.aprs2.net:14580.

options.name: --region
options.description: Regional rotate: noam, soam, euro, asia or aunz. Cannot be combined with --server.

options.name: --port
options.description: TCP port, for --region or a --server without a port. Default: 14580.

options.name: --full-feed
options.description: Use the full feed port (10152). All traffic, so expect a heavy stream. [default: False]

options.name: --tls
options.description: Connect over TLS, checking the server's certificate. Default server: ssl.aprs2.net:24580; a --server without a port uses 24580. Few servers offer TLS. Cannot be combined with --region or --full-feed. [default: False]

options.name: --filter
options.description: APRS-IS filter sent with the login, for example "r/35/-97/200" or "t/m".

options.name: --timestamps
options.description: Prefix each printed line with a UTC timestamp. [default: False]

options.name: --capture
options.description: Append every packet to this file as "<UTC timestamp> <raw line>". The directory is created if needed.

options.name: --quiet
options.description: Do not print packets to the console (useful with --capture). [default: False]

options.name: --log-packets
options.description: Also log every packet to OpenTelemetry. Needs OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT. Never written to the console. [default: False]

options.name: --count
options.description: Stop after this many packets.

options.name: --duration
options.description: Stop after this long, for example 90s, 10m, 2h or 1d.

options.name: --reconnect
options.description: If the connection drops or the server goes silent for 90s, reconnect (waiting 5s, doubling to 60s) and keep going until --count, --duration or Ctrl+C. Only after the first login succeeds. [default: False]

options.name: --max-silence
options.description: Treat the connection as failed after this long with no packets, even if the server still sends keepalives (its feed may have stalled). Default: 10m with --reconnect, otherwise off. Use 'off' to disable.

options.name: --stats
options.description: Print a summary to standard error this often, for example 1m, and once at the end: packets by type, malformed, unsupported and messages to your callsign.

options.name: --format
options.description: Console output: raw (the line as received), decoded (one readable line of decoded fields), json (one JSON object per line) or pretty (a labelled block per packet). Capture files are always raw. [default: raw]

options.name: --color
options.description: Colour for --format pretty: auto (only on a terminal, and not when NO_COLOR is set), always or never. [default: auto]

commands.name: passcode
commands.description: Print the APRS-IS passcode for a callsign, for a verified login. Only for your own licensed callsign.

arguments.name: CALLSIGN
arguments.description: Callsign, with or without an SSID. The SSID and letter case do not change the passcode.

commands.name: parse
commands.description: Decode APRS packets and print their fields.

options.name: --file
options.description: Read packets from this file, one per line. Capture files from listen --capture work too.

options.name: --format
options.description: Output: pretty (default, a labelled block per packet), decoded (one line per packet) or json (one JSON object per line). [default: pretty]

options.name: --color
options.description: Colour for --format pretty: auto (only on a terminal, and not when NO_COLOR is set), always or never. [default: auto]

arguments.name: PACKET
arguments.description: Packets in TNC2 format (SOURCE>DEST,PATH:INFO). Quote each one. Without any, lines are read from --file or standard input.

commands.name: replay
commands.description: Run captured packets through the parser and report outcomes, packet types, issues and undecoded types.

options.name: --examples
options.description: Example lines to show for each issue and undecoded data type. 0 hides them. Default: 3. [default: 3]

options.name: --format
options.description: Report format: text (default) or json. [default: text]

arguments.name: FILES
arguments.description: Capture files (from listen --capture) or files of raw lines. Use - for standard input.

commands.name: send
commands.description: Send a status report, message, position, object, weather or telemetry report to APRS-IS. Needs your callsign and its passcode.

options.name: --callsign
options.description: Your callsign, with optional SSID, as the sender and the login. Required.

options.name: --passcode
options.description: APRS-IS passcode for the callsign. Prefer the APRS_PASSCODE environment variable; an option value is visible in the process list and your shell history. Never printed or logged.

options.name: --server
options.description: Server as host[:port]. Default: rotate.aprs2.net:14580.

options.name: --region
options.description: Regional rotate: noam, soam, euro, asia or aunz. Cannot be combined with --server.

options.name: --tls
options.description: Connect over TLS, checking the server's certificate. Default server: ssl.aprs2.net:24580; a --server without a port uses 24580. Cannot be combined with --region. [default: False]

options.name: --tocall
options.description: Destination TOCALL that identifies the software. Default: APZNET (experimental). [default: APZNET]

options.name: --path
options.description: Digipeater path, comma-separated, for example WIDE1-1. Default: none (APRS-IS only).

options.name: --dry-run
options.description: Print the packet that would be sent, without connecting. [default: False]

commands.name: status
commands.description: Send a status report.

commands.name: message
commands.description: Send a message and wait for the recipient's acknowledgement, resending it until then (see --retry). Replies are acknowledged and printed.

options.name: --wait-replies
options.description: After the message is answered, keep listening this long for replies, acknowledging and printing each, for example 30s or 5m. 0 stops at once. Default: 2m. [default: 2m]

options.name: --retry
options.description: How the message is resent until it is acknowledged: default (30 s, 1, 2, 4 and 8 minutes), aprs-is (30 s, 2 and 5 minutes), slow-hf (2, 4, 8 and 16 minutes) or none (once). Default: default. [default: default]

arguments.name: ADDRESSEE
arguments.description: Callsign to send the message to.

commands.name: position
commands.description: Send a position report.

options.name: --lat
options.description: Latitude in degrees, north positive.

options.name: --lon
options.description: Longitude in degrees, east positive.

options.name: --symbol
options.description: Symbol as table and code, for example /> (car) or /- (house). Default: /- . [default: /-]

options.name: --comment
options.description: Comment after the position.

commands.name: object
commands.description: Send an object, timestamped now; --kill removes it.

options.name: --lat
options.description: Latitude in degrees, north positive.

options.name: --lon
options.description: Longitude in degrees, east positive.

options.name: --symbol
options.description: Symbol as table and code, for example /> (car) or /- (house). Default: /- . [default: /-]

options.name: --comment
options.description: Comment after the position.

options.name: --kill
options.description: Send the object as killed, to remove it. [default: False]

commands.name: weather
commands.description: Send weather readings: a complete report with --lat and --lon, otherwise a positionless one. Readings left out are sent as unknown (wind, gust, temperature) or not at all.

options.name: --lat
options.description: Station latitude. With --lon, sends a complete report; without, a positionless one.

options.name: --lon
options.description: Station longitude.

options.name: --symbol
options.description: Weather station symbol, /_ or \_ with an overlay. Default: /_ . [default: /_]

options.name: --wind-dir
options.description: Wind direction, degrees.

options.name: --wind-speed
options.description: Sustained wind speed, mph.

options.name: --gust
options.description: Peak wind in the last 5 minutes, mph.

options.name: --temp
options.description: Temperature, °F.

options.name: --rain-1h
options.description: Rain in the last hour, inches.

options.name: --rain-24h
options.description: Rain in the last 24 hours, inches.

options.name: --rain-midnight
options.description: Rain since local midnight, inches.

options.name: --humidity
options.description: Relative humidity, 1 to 100 %.

options.name: --pressure
options.description: Barometric pressure, millibars.

options.name: --luminosity
options.description: Luminosity, W/m².

options.name: --snow
options.description: Snowfall in the last 24 hours, inches. Needs --lat and --lon.

options.name: --comment
options.description: Comment after the position.

commands.name: telemetry
commands.description: Send a telemetry report (T#), after any PARM./UNIT./EQNS./BITS. definitions given, which go to your own callsign.

options.name: --seq
options.description: Telemetry sequence number, 0 to 999. Required.

options.name: --analog
options.description: One to five raw analog values, whole numbers 0 to 999, comma-separated: 199,0,255,73,123.

options.name: --digital
options.description: The eight digital channels as 0s and 1s: 01101001. Needs all five analog values.

options.name: --comment
options.description: Comment after the position.

options.name: --names
options.description: Also send PARM.: channel names, comma-separated, analog then digital.

options.name: --units
options.description: Also send UNIT.: channel units or labels, comma-separated, analog then digital.

options.name: --equations
options.description: Also send EQNS.: a,b,c per analog channel (reading = a·v² + b·v + c), channels separated by ';'.

options.name: --bits
options.description: Also send BITS.: the 'on' state of each digital channel as eight 0s and 1s.

options.name: --project
options.description: Project name sent with --bits.

commands.name: tnc
commands.description: Talk to a KISS TNC over TCP, such as Dire Wolf, or on a serial port.

commands.name: listen
commands.description: Connect to a KISS TNC and print the APRS packets it hears.

options.name: --tnc
options.description: The TNC as host[:port] (default port 8001, Dire Wolf's KISS port), or a serial TNC as serial:PORT[@BAUD], such as serial:/dev/ttyUSB0 or serial:COM3@57600 (default 9600 baud).

options.name: --radio-port
options.description: The radio port on a multi-port TNC, 0 to 15. Default: 0. [default: 0]

options.name: --format
options.description: Output: raw (the TNC2 line), decoded, json or pretty, as for listen. [default: raw]

options.name: --count
options.description: Stop after this many packets.

options.name: --duration
options.description: Stop after this long, for example 90s, 10m, 2h or 1d.

options.name: --reconnect
options.description: If the TNC closes the connection, is unplugged or cannot be reached, keep trying (waiting 5s, doubling to 60s; 2s to 30s for a serial port) until --count, --duration or Ctrl+C. Without it, the first loss ends the command. [default: False]

options.name: --quiet-warning
options.description: Warn when the TNC sends nothing at all for this long, for example 10m: it may be switched off behind a port that stays open. Pick longer than the channel is ever quiet. Needs --reconnect. Default: off.

commands.name: send
commands.description: Transmit a status report, message, position, object, weather or telemetry report on the air through a KISS TNC. Needs your callsign and a licence to transmit; check the path first with --dry-run.

options.name: --callsign
options.description: Your callsign, with optional SSID, as the sender and the login. Required.

options.name: --tnc
options.description: The TNC as host[:port]. Default port: 8001 (Dire Wolf's KISS port).

options.name: --radio-port
options.description: The radio port on a multi-port TNC, 0 to 15. Default: 0. [default: 0]

options.name: --tocall
options.description: Destination TOCALL that identifies the software. Default: APZNET (experimental). [default: APZNET]

options.name: --path
options.description: Digipeater path, comma-separated. Default: WIDE1-1,WIDE2-1; use "" for none (direct only).

options.name: --dry-run
options.description: Print the packet that would be transmitted, without connecting to the TNC. [default: False]

commands.name: ports
commands.description: List the serial ports present, for --tnc serial:PORT.

commands.name: serve
commands.description: Serve an APRS-IS feed, KISS TNCs or both to local APRS-IS clients, each with its own filter. A packet heard on several sources is served once. Clients are read-only.

options.name: --callsign
options.description: Callsign for the read-only upstream login, with optional SSID. Default: a listener ID such as SWL482913.

options.name: --server
options.description: Upstream APRS-IS server as host[:port]. Default: rotate.aprs2.net:14580.

options.name: --filter
options.description: Upstream APRS-IS filter: everything local clients can ask for, for example "r/35/-97/300". Each client then narrows it with its own filter. Without it, only the --tnc sources are served.

options.name: --tnc
options.description: Also serve what a KISS TNC hears, as host[:port] (default port 8001, Dire Wolf's) or serial:PORT[@BAUD] for a TNC on a serial port. Repeat for several TNCs. A lost or unplugged TNC is reconnected.

options.name: --listen
options.description: Address and port to serve on. Default: 127.0.0.1:14580 (this computer only); use 0.0.0.0:14580 to serve your network. [default: 127.0.0.1:14580]

options.name: --http
options.description: Also serve HTTP on this address:port, for example 127.0.0.1:14590: WebSocket clients at ws://address:port/aprs get JSON packets and set their filter in the URL or a message, and /health says whether each source is connected (503 when none is). Default: off.

options.name: --name
options.description: Server name sent to clients: 1 to 9 letters, digits or '-'. Default: APRSNET. [default: APRSNET]

options.name: --history
options.description: Send each client the packets from this long before it connected, for example 10m. Default: off.

options.name: --duration
options.description: Stop after this long, for example 2h. Default: until Ctrl+C.

options.name: --quiet-warning
options.description: Warn when a --tnc sends nothing at all for this long, for example 10m: it may be switched off behind a port that stays open. Pick longer than the channel is ever quiet. /health shows it as quiet. Default: off.

commands.name: health
commands.description: Check a running 'aprscli serve --http': prints its health report and exits 0 while any source is connected, 1 when none is, 2 when it doesn't answer.

options.name: --timeout
options.description: How long to wait for an answer, for example 5s. Default: 5s. [default: 5s]

arguments.name: URL
arguments.description: The health URL of aprscli serve --http. Default: http://127.0.0.1:14590/health. [default: http://127.0.0.1:14590/health]
